taskTitle: Where ten HTTP header fields are defined

checks.detail: 0 state changes, each allowed by a review (0 reviews in all)
1 phase had the tools designed for them

finalText:
I found the defining section for all ten header fields and read each one on rfc-editor.org. Two RFCs cover eight of them. RFC 9111 (HTTP Caching) defines Age, Cache-Control and Expires. RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) defines Last-Modified, ETag, Location, Retry-After and Vary. The other two come from RFC 6797 (Strict-Transport-Security) and RFC 8288 (Link).

**Is each RFC still current?** My check here is limited. I searched each page for "Obsoleted by", which would appear in the RFC's header if a later RFC had replaced it.
- RFC 9110 matched only in its own section listing the specifications it replaces (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html).
- RFC 9111 had no match (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html).
- RFC 6797 matched only an unrelated sentence about other specifications. I searched for the word "Obsolete" there, which is broader, so it would also have caught "Obsoleted by" (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6797.html).
- RFC 8288's header says "Obsoletes: 5988" and has no "Obsoleted by" line (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288.html).

I didn't check the RFC Editor's separate status pages.

**Where each field is defined**
- **Age:** RFC 9111 §5.1 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html)
- **Cache-Control:** RFC 9111 §5.2
- **Expires:** RFC 9111 §5.3
- **Last-Modified:** RFC 9110 §8.8.2 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)
- **ETag:** RFC 9110 §8.8.3
- **Location:** RFC 9110 §10.2.2
- **Retry-After:** RFC 9110 §10.2.3
- **Vary:** RFC 9110 §12.5.5
- **Strict-Transport-Security:** RFC 6797 §6.1, "Strict-Transport-Security HTTP Response Header Field" (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6797.html)
- **Link:** RFC 8288 §3, "Link Serialisation in HTTP Headers" (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288.html)

The RFC pages wrap lines at a fixed width. Each quote below is one continuous sentence, with the line breaks replaced by single spaces.
